[[Category:Linear map]][[Category:Matrix]]
Let $\mathbf{A}$ be a [[linear map]] or a [[matrix]].

If for $\vec v \neq 0$:

$$
\mathbf{A}\vec v = \lambda \vec v,
$$

Then:

$\vec v$ is an '''eigenvector''' of $\mathbf{A}$, and $\lambda$ is the associated '''eigenvalue'''.

<blockquote>
An '''eigenvector''' is a nonzero vector that is scaled by $\mathbf{A}$ according to the '''eigenvalue''' but not rotated in direction.
</blockquote>

== Properties ==

=== $(\mathbf{A}-\lambda \mathbf{I})\vec v=0$ ===

i.e., any '''eigenvector''' $\vec v$ is in the [[linear map#Kernel|kernel]] of [[linear map]] $\mathbf{A}-\lambda \mathbf{I}$.
